issues.reason: The superlative is specified as (Most <scale> X <class>) 'plus X is a member of the class', and a group of sentences cannot satisfy that membership, so putting sk_group_1 in the ranked-individual slot is ill-typed and asserts the group is itself the single simplest sentence.

The group-in-entity-slot half stands exactly as in the first issue, but the absent identity atom is the equative coverage gap (no form exists for 'the Xs are the Ys'), not a parse defect — the shared symbol is the only available carrier.

gaps_confirmed: identity / equative copular clause between two definite descriptions has no form
plural superlative — the set of top-ranked members — has no form (Most ranks a single entity in a class)
plural one-anaphora ('the ... ones') as a predicate nominal is uncovered
new_gaps: definite plural with generic/aphoristic force — the determiner rule mandates a specific-group reading, leaving no kind-level generic route for 'the Xs are the Ys' aphorisms
repair_summary: Re-expressed each superlative through the licensed definite-plural distribution rule — (Implication (PartOf $x sk_group_1) (Most simple $x sentence)) and likewise for elegant, each (STV 1.0 0.9) — so Most's entity slot holds a member sentence, not the group.
notes: The distribution rules follow the stated pattern for copular predicates over a definite plural group; the identity of the two descriptions remains carried only by the shared group symbol pending the equative gap.
